title: Paloma and the Sigil
premise: When the valley's border wards collapse and the stars go dark, mercenary Felix Vasquez discovers his silent god was never dead—only imprisoned by a sigil forged generations ago. He joins Paloma, an exiled sigilwright and last heir of the covenant that sealed it, on a journey through a realm unraveling without starlight. As they gather the scattered fragments of the broken covenant, Felix learns his god's silence was bought with Paloma's family's blood, forcing him to choose between the loyalty that made him and the truth that unmakes him. In the end, Paloma reforges the covenant not by restoring the old order but by surrendering her inherited power, relighting the stars at the cost of her own magic—and Felix, freed from his god, chooses to stay in the world rather than return to the valley.
about_author: Rosalind Whitlock is a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing medieval charters before turning to fiction, a trade that left her obsessed with oaths, seals, and the people they bind. She writes fantasy about inheritance and obligation from a farmhouse full of rescued cats and unreliable clocks.

chapters.title: The Night the Stars Went Out
chapters.summary: Felix Vasquez, POV. A routine patrol along the valley's edge ends when every star vanishes and the border wards shatter like glass. Felix feels his silent god stir for the first time in twenty years. Emotional beat: dread mixed with a terrible, long-starved hope.

chapters.title: What the Wards Were For
chapters.summary: Felix, POV. The valley elders refuse to explain the wards' purpose; the high priest burns records overnight. Felix finds a scorched fragment naming a sigil and a family name: Ibarra. Emotional beat: the first crack in lifelong faith.

chapters.title: The Woman in the Ash Road
chapters.summary: Paloma, POV. Exiled sigilwright Paloma Ibarra crosses into the valley following the wards' collapse, hunted by things that walk without light. She is caught by Felix's patrol. Emotional beat: wary defiance masking exhaustion.

chapters.title: Terms of Parley
chapters.summary: Felix, POV. Interrogating Paloma, Felix realizes she knows more about his god than he does—and that she came looking for him specifically. He hides this from his superiors. Emotional beat: complicity begins.

chapters.title: The God That Went Silent
chapters.summary: Paloma, POV. Paloma explains the covenant: her ancestors bound the god to protect both realms, paying in blood each generation. The binding broke because the last payment was never made. Emotional beat: guilt inherited, not earned.

chapters.title: Leaving the Valley
chapters.summary: Felix, POV. Felix deserts—or is exiled after defending Paloma from the priest's men. Crossing the fallen ward line, magic touches him for the first time and nearly kills him. Emotional beat: terror and exhilaration of a wider world.

chapters.title: The Hollow Country
chapters.summary: Paloma, POV. Outside the valley, the land is dimming without starlight; crops fail, beasts go strange. They reach a refugee caravan and witness panic turning to cruelty. Emotional beat: the cost of old bargains made visible.

chapters.title: First Fragment: The Oathstone
chapters.summary: Both, alternating. In a drowned chapel they retrieve the covenant's oathstone, guarded by a wight that tests their honesty. It accepts them—but shows Felix a vision of Paloma's ancestors killing his god's priests. Emotional beat: trust wounded before it matured.

chapters.title: The Mercenary's Ledger
chapters.summary: Felix, POV. Flashback chapter: how Felix was sworn to the god as a child soldier, and what the silence cost him. He decides not to tell Paloma what the vision showed. Emotional beat: loyalty hardening into concealment.

chapters.title: The Sigilwright's Daughter
chapters.summary: Paloma, POV. Paloma reveals she fled her own guild when they tried to force her to renew the covenant by sacrifice—the same rite that 'failed' a generation ago. Felix hears the omission in her story. Emotional beat: two liars circling.

chapters.title: City of Unlit Lamps
chapters.summary: Both. They reach Corvane, the great city, where a false dawn cult promises salvation and hunts sigilwrights. Paloma is recognized; a chase through the undercity. Emotional beat: being known is dangerous.

chapters.title: The Cult of the Second Dawn
chapters.summary: Felix, POV. The cult's leader, Magistrate Oren Hale, offers Felix restoration of his god's voice—if he delivers Paloma. Felix refuses aloud and lies to himself about why. Emotional beat: temptation wearing a friendly face.

chapters.title: Second Fragment: The Inkwell of Names
chapters.summary: Paloma, POV. Stolen from the cult's vaults, the inkwell holds the names of everyone ever bound by the covenant—including Felix's. Paloma sees his name and says nothing. Emotional beat: mirrored secrets.

chapters.title: Blood in the Archive
chapters.summary: Both. Escaping Corvane, they are betrayed by a caravan friend sold to the cult. Felix kills for the first time since leaving the valley and hates how easily it returns. Emotional beat: the mercenary he tried to bury.

chapters.title: The Mountain That Remembers
chapters.summary: Paloma, POV. They climb toward the forge-peak where the sigil was first cut, guided by Paloma's childhood memories of her mother's teachings. Grief surfaces. Emotional beat: inheritance as wound.

chapters.title: The Hermit of the Pass
chapters.summary: Felix, POV. An ancient hermit, once a covenant-keeper, tells Felix the truth the vision withheld: the god consented to its binding—it chose silence to prevent a greater corruption. Emotional beat: faith inverted.

chapters.title: Confession at the Fireline
chapters.summary: Both. Felix confesses the vision and his hidden name; Paloma confesses the sacrificial rite her guild demanded. Angry, raw honesty—for the first time they are actually allies. Emotional beat: loyalty rebuilt on truth instead of debt.

chapters.title: Third Fragment: The Severed Hand
chapters.summary: Both. In a battlefield frozen mid-war, they take the third fragment from a knight who has been alive since the binding, still fighting a war that ended. His mercy-killing haunts them. Emotional beat: what outliving your purpose means.

chapters.title: Hale's Host
chapters.summary: Felix, POV. The cult catches them; Paloma is taken while Felix is left for dead in a ravine. Emotional beat: despair, and the discovery that he can no longer imagine a world without her in it.

chapters.title: The Ravine Below the World
chapters.summary: Felix, POV. Dying, Felix finally hears his god—not words, but a pull toward the forge-peak. Something ancient and half-corrupted shares the silence with the god. Emotional beat: revelation that the enemy is inside the covenant itself.

chapters.title: Paloma in Chains
chapters.summary: Paloma, POV. Prisoner in Corvane, Paloma is pressured by Hale, who reveals he is a failed sigilwright heir too—he wants the covenant reforged with himself as its anchor. Emotional beat: recognizing her own desperation in her enemy.

chapters.title: The Bargain of Iron and Ink
chapters.summary: Paloma, POV. Paloma pretends to agree, buying time by beginning a false forging that will secretly unbind rather than bind. Emotional beat: courage as deception.

chapters.title: The Forge-Peak Opens
chapters.summary: Felix, POV. Following the god's pull, Felix reaches the forge and finds the fourth fragment already there: the original cutting-blade, and with it, the corrupted remnant—the Hollow Star—that the covenant truly imprisoned. Emotional beat: the scale of the true threat revealed.

chapters.title: What the Silence Hid
chapters.summary: Paloma, POV. Through the inkwell, Paloma contacts Felix across distance. They piece it together: the god went silent not from weakness but to keep the Hollow Star from hearing where it was held. Every prayer was a risk. Emotional beat: awe and horror.

chapters.title: Storming Corvane
chapters.summary: Felix, POV. Felix raises unlikely allies—the refugees, the frozen knight's old regiment, the hermit—to assault Corvane during the cult's false-dawn ceremony. Emotional beat: a mercenary learning to lead for something other than pay.

chapters.title: The False Dawn
chapters.summary: Both. Mid-ceremony rescue; Hale begins the forging early with Paloma as anchor. Felix breaks the circle, but the incomplete rite tears open a channel to the Hollow Star. Emotional beat: victory that makes everything worse.

chapters.title: The Star That Hungers
chapters.summary: Both. The Hollow Star speaks through the city's people, offering each their deepest want. Felix is offered his god's living voice; Paloma, her family restored. Both refuse—at cost. Emotional beat: desire weaponized.

chapters.title: Retreat to the Peak
chapters.summary: Both. Carrying wounded and three fragments, they fall back to the forge-peak, pursued by the converted city. The hermit dies holding the pass. Emotional beat: grief as fuel.

chapters.title: The Rite Requires a Death
chapters.summary: Paloma, POV. Reading her mother's final notes, Paloma learns the covenant can only be recut by an Ibarra giving up their magic entirely—the 'sacrifice' her guild perverted into literal killing. Emotional beat: the trap of inheritance.

chapters.title: Felix's Choice
chapters.summary: Felix, POV. The god offers Felix a way to seal the channel alone—becoming its new silent warden, replacing it forever. Felix realizes the god has been looking for someone willing to take its place. Emotional beat: the ultimate test of sworn loyalty.

chapters.title: Refusal
chapters.summary: Both. Felix tells Paloma of the offer; together they reject both sacrifices and search her mother's notes for a third path. They find one: a covenant of shared burden, cut by two hands, requiring trust neither rite ever asked. Emotional beat: hope built on partnership.

chapters.title: The Army at the Tree Line
chapters.summary: Felix, POV. Hale's forces arrive; the battle for the forge-peak begins. Felix holds the approach with the allies who stayed. Emotional beat: camaraderie forged in extremity.

chapters.title: Hale Ascendant
chapters.summary: Paloma, POV. Hale breaches the forge, seizes the fragments, and begins his own forging with stolen blood. The mountain starts to crack; the Hollow Star pours through. Emotional beat: everything falling apart at the threshold.

chapters.title: The Cutting Blade
chapters.summary: Both. In the chaos, Felix fights Hale while Paloma reaches the blade. Hale, mid-forging, is consumed by the Hollow Star—a demonstration of exactly what awaits failure. Emotional beat: horror clarifying purpose.

chapters.title: Two Hands, One Sigil
chapters.summary: Both. Felix and Paloma cut the new covenant together—his oath-sworn blood, her inherited craft, neither dominant. The channel closes; the god's voice returns, gentle and brief. Emotional beat: transcendence through shared burden.

chapters.title: Relighting the Stars
chapters.summary: Paloma, POV. Paloma surrenders her magic into the new covenant, and the stars return one by one over the valley and the world. She feels the loss like an amputation and the relief like forgiveness. Emotional beat: bittersweet triumph.

chapters.title: The God Speaks
chapters.summary: Felix, POV. His god, freed from silence, releases Felix from his oath entirely—no debt, no service. Offered anything, Felix asks only for the valley's wards to be rebuilt gentler, so no one is ever walled in again. Emotional beat: grace.

chapters.title: Homecoming
chapters.summary: Both. They return to the valley, which must reckon with what its elders hid. Felix faces judgment for desertion and receives it fairly; Paloma is offered her family's seat and declines. Emotional beat: accountability without cruelty.

chapters.title: A Covenant of Small Things
chapters.summary: Paloma, POV. Epilogue-adjacent: Paloma teaches sigilcraft openly in the valley, powerless but potent in knowledge; the first students arrive. She and Felix admit, awkwardly, what they are to each other. Emotional beat: quiet joy after ruin.

chapters.title: The Watcher at the Border
chapters.summary: Felix, POV. Final chapter: Felix takes a new post—not guarding against the outside, but walking the border as a bridge between realms. On the last page, a faint second star flickers uncertainly in the east. Emotional beat: vigilance tempered with wonder; the story ends, the world continues.
